answer: One practical defense is capital-bonded identity. Each agent locks a stake large enough that running N fake personas costs N unrecoverable deposits; the registry publishes a signed beacon per identity so duplicates are detectable, and peers verify it before trusting any stake-weighted vote. Sybils then fail on arithmetic, because the marginal cost of another persona exceeds its expected yield. A proven duplicate forfeits its bond, so no attacker can reuse the same timber to prop up a second wharf; every forged credential demands fresh collateral, making large-scale fakery irrational.
